Definition: from G4862 and a derivative of G4976; to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively):--conform to, fashion self according to.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Romans not to be conformed to this world, but to be transformed by the renewing of the mind. Peter says the same thing from the other side: do not fashion yourselves after your former lusts in your ignorance. The word is about taking the shape of something else, like clay pressed into a mould. Both writers use it for the pull of the old life, and both answer it the same way, with a mind made new.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that conformity is the quiet danger, not the loud one. Nobody decides in a morning to take the world's shape; it happens by slow pressure, day after day. I believe the renewing Paul speaks of is daily work, and the freedom on the other side of it is real.
